# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 65 (Bi-Vb Pc65)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc65
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 65
**Title (English, from literature):** Ordaining a married girl under twelve
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 65 (*Ūnadvādasavassa-gihigata*) governs the full ordination of a formerly married girl (*gihigatā*), decreeing that a nun who ordains such a girl younger than twelve years of age commits an offence requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [Bodhi; Hüsken 1997]. In the Theravāda Vinaya, monastic law distinguishes female candidates according to their marital status, prescribing twelve years as the minimum age for a married girl, whereas unmarried maidens (*kumāribhūtā*, regulated in Pācittiya 71) must be at least twenty years of age; together, these two rules correspond functionally to the single monk rule (Bhikkhu Pācittiya 65), which sets a general age threshold of twenty without regard to marriage [Hüsken 1997]. Although some early translations construed *ūnadvādasavassa* as referring to a woman married for twelve years, modern scholarship and textual authorities treat it as chronological age [Hüsken 1997]. The commentary (*Samantapāsādikā*) clarifies that if a preceptor confers ordination under the mistaken belief that the girl has reached the full twelve years, she is free from offence (*anāpatti*), but the candidate nevertheless remains unordained (*anupasampannā*), because ordaining a married girl under twelve can never constitute a valid formal act (*dhammakamma*) [Bodhi; Hüsken 1997].

 Algorithmic alignment by DharmaNexus reveals substantial Pali-internal phraseological reuse, particularly with the parallel ordination rule for maidens (Bi-Vb Pc 71, sharing over 4,500 characters across §1.14–2.3.6), neighboring Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga ordination rules (Pc 61–63, Pc 66–67, Pc 72, Pc 74–75, Pc 82), the monk rule Bu-Vb Pc 65, the Mahākhandhaka (Kd 1), and formulaic legal text in the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 4, AN 5) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-language matches with Tibetan translations of the Vinayavastu and the *Vinayasūtravṛtti* [DharmaNexus].
